reuse.why: Fintegra linking reuses linkBankSyncAccount and findOrCreateBank, but the takeover re-implements unlinkAccount's field reset inline and downloadFintegraTransactions is a copy of downloadAkahuTransactions instead of a shared provider-download helper.

duplication.why: The holder query is written twice (in assertBankAccountNotLinked and in linkBankSyncAccount), the unlink column reset copies unlinkAccount, the Fintegra download copies the Akahu one line for line, and the assert call plus flag threading is repeated in all six provider functions.

placement.why: Rules sit in accounts/app.ts next to linkBankSyncAccount and the download in sync.ts beside the other providers, though the checks live in each provider wrapper rather than in the shared linking path.

scope.why: Changes stay on linking, Fintegra and the takeover flag; the desktop-client edits are the minimum needed for the provider union, plus release notes.

maintainability.why: assertBankAccountNotLinked now also enforces the closed-account rule and takes a bypass flag, so its name misleads, and every new provider must remember both the assert call and the flag pass-through.

bypasses_abstraction.where: linkBankSyncAccount's replaceExistingLink branch clears the holder's bank columns with its own db.updateAccount instead of going through the existing unlinkAccount logic (or a provider-free part of it).

disguised_duplication.where: The 'other holder' lookup is reshaped (first vs all) between assertBankAccountNotLinked and linkBankSyncAccount, and downloadFintegraTransactions is the Akahu download renamed.

abstraction_drift.where: linkBankSyncAccount gains replaceExistingLink with an inline unlink branch; assertBankAccountNotLinked gains replaceExistingLink and an unrelated closed-account branch; the inline unlink bypasses unlinkAccount.
